title: Pide peynirli
subtitle: Turkish flatbread boat with cheese filling
excerpt: Pide peynirli are boat-shaped Turkish flatbreads filled with a mix of white cheese, mozzarella, and egg, baked until the bread is golden and the filling bubbles and sets. They come out of the oven crisp at the edges and molten at the centre.
sourceNotes: Aylin Oney Tan, A Taste of Sun and Fire: Gaziantep Cookery (2014). Pide documented as one of the defining breads of Turkish cuisine, with regional variations across the Black Sea coast and central Anatolia. Paula Wolfert, The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean (1994). The pide dough method and cheese filling described.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerated after the first rise. Shape and fill just before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 220 degrees / gas 9. Preheat for at least 30 minutes.

content.text: Pide are Turkish flatbreads shaped into boats with pinched ends, filled and baked at very high heat so the bread cooks in minutes and the filling goes golden and molten. The cheese version uses feta for salt and mozzarella for melt, with an egg cracked in at the last minute. They need a very hot oven and should be eaten the moment they come out.

Mix {{yeast-dried}} and {{caster-sugar}} into 260 ml of warm water and leave five minutes until foamy. Combine {{strong-bread-flour}} and {{sea-salt-fine}} in a bowl. Add the yeast liquid and {{olive-oil}}, mix to a rough dough, then knead for eight minutes until smooth. Cover and prove for one hour until doubled.

Preheat the oven to 240 degrees. Divide the dough into four pieces. On a floured surface, roll each piece into an oval about 30 cm long. Pinch the two ends into points to form a boat shape and roll the edges up slightly to contain the filling.
Mix {{feta}} and {{mozzarella}} together and divide among the four pide, spreading it within the raised edge. Transfer to baking trays.

Bake for eight minutes until the cheese is melted and beginning to brown. Crack one {{eggs}} into the centre of each pide. Bake for a further four to five minutes until the egg white is just set but the yolk is still runny. Brush the edges with {{unsalted-butter}} if using and grind {{black-pepper}} over. Eat immediately.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough or tray not preheated
items.fix: Pide needs an extremely hot oven. Preheat the baking trays so the base starts cooking the moment the pide goes on.

items.symptom: The filling runs out over the sides
items.cause: Edges not rolled up high enough
items.fix: Roll the dough edges up by at least 1 cm all around and pinch the ends firmly. The shape should hold its own.

items.cause: Added too early or oven too hot
items.fix: Add the egg only after the cheese is fully melted. Watch it carefully: the egg only needs four minutes at most.

items.symptom: The cheese mixture is too salty
items.fix: Soak the crumbled feta in cold water for twenty minutes before using to reduce the salt level.

content.text: Pide is the Turkish flatbread tradition distinct from lahmacun (thin, round) and ekmek (loaf bread). Pide shops (pideci) are found all over Turkey and serve the full range of fillings: cheese, egg, minced lamb, sucuk (spiced beef sausage), and mixed versions. The Black Sea region is particularly associated with pide and has its own style, with a thicker dough and richer cheese filling using local kas cheese. Peynirli pide (cheese pide) is one of the most ordered versions. In Istanbul, pide shops often run alongside grilled meat restaurants and are open late into the night.
